source.title: Letter 187
source.breadcrumbs: Home > Fathers of the Church > Letters (St. Basil of Caesarea) > Letter 187

paragraphs.text: <quote>Twice cabbage is death,</quote> says the unkind proverb. I, however, though I have called for it often, shall die once. Yes: even though I had never called for it at all! If you do die anyhow, don't fear to eat a delicious relish, unjustly reviled by the proverb!

source.source_note: Source. Translated by Blomfield Jackson. From Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, Vol. 8. Edited by Philip Schaff and Henry Wace. latex.p0004: \Quote{两次白菜便是死，}刻薄的谚语说。而我，虽常呼唤它，却将死一次。是的：即使我从未呼唤过它！若你无论如何都要死，就不要害怕品尝一道美味佳肴，尽管被那谚语不公地诋毁！
